title: Existing native quasi-finite punctual weight calculation
statement: Let k₀ be a finite field, l a different prime, ι : PadicAlgCl l →+* ℂ, and f : X → Y a separated, locally quasi-finite, locally finite-type, quasi-compact morphism over k₀. Assume Y is locally finite type, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over k₀. For a native Weil sheaf F on X, R⁰f!F preserves both punctual upper weight bounds and punctual purity of any real weight w [def-weil-punctual-weights]. No absolute separatedness of X or Y, and no surjectivity of ι, is needed.

proof.text: Use compact-support base change and composition from [prop-functor-package] at Spec κ(y). The fibre is finite, so its compactly supported cohomology is concentrated in degree zero. The Frobenius trace formula [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] on that fibre determines its reverse characteristic polynomial as the product of the expanded local reverse characteristic polynomials. This is implemented, without local sorry, by exists_charpolyRev_stalk_higherLowerShriek_zero in QuasiFiniteStalk.lean.

The root of a factor expanded by e gives a nonzero e and a closed x above y for which β^e is an eigenvalue of F_x and deg(x)=deg(y)*e. This is the proved source theorem exists_hasEigenvalue_stalk_of_hasEigenvalue_stalk_higherLowerShriek_zero. Hence q_x=q_y^e. The upper bound (respectively purity) in [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives ‖ι(β)‖^e ≤ (q_y^(w/2))^e (respectively equality); injectivity and order reflection of positive integral powers on nonnegative real numbers gives the result. The source proofs use pow_le_natCast_pow_rpow_iff and pow_eq_natCast_pow_rpow_iff. Zero fibres have no eigenvalues.
